problem:
Consider the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}{x}_{2} \\ {e}^{{x}_{1}{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

If the linear approximation of $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}∗ \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & ∗ \\ ∗ & 2\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}]),
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?

activity_context.topic_title: The Derivative of a Multivariable Function

feedback.problem:
Consider the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{-1} \\ {x}_{1}{x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

If the linear approximation of $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}∗ \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ \\ \frac{1}{2} & 2\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]),
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{-1})=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{-1})=-{x}_{2}^{-2} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2})={x}_{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2})={x}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -{x}_{2}^{-2} \\ {x}_{2} & {x}_{1}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 2\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
4+1+(-4)=1.
$$
